A1.justification: Both PDFs present The Limits of Tractable Marginalization. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions and proofs, including its appendices. Figure 2 and the numerical examples illustrate mathematical calculations rather than original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical presentation and illustrative calculations. Neither the main text nor the appendices report experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: The UFMAC model and the procedures for ordinary, Hamming-weight, and virtual-evidence marginalization remain unchanged in Sections 2–5 and Appendices A–C.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmarks for training or evaluation. The theoretical problems and illustrative binary-variable examples are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. Models such as DPPs and SPNs retain their theoretical role; the added Ahmed et al. citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental evaluation protocols. The inputs and conditions of the worked marginalization examples remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical supplementary analyses. The worked examples and appendix arguments are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The numerical examples are unchanged: Example 3.2 yields 0.25, and Examples 4.2 and 4.6 yield 0.16. Figure 2 retains the same probabilities, and no empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, constructions, and proofs are unchanged, including Theorem 4.10, Proposition 5.4, and Corollary D.1. Appendices A–D contain the same mathematical arguments.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that known circuit representations do not capture all tractable marginalization under FP != #P, and establish completeness for virtual-evidence marginalization in the real-RAM setting. Their scope and qualifications remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the separating function, virtual evidence, and the restriction of completeness to real RAMs are retained. The final open question still concerns limits of parallelization; its revised terminology does not introduce a new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: The circuit representation details in Appendix A.1 and real-RAM specification in Appendix C are unchanged. No implementation, reproducibility, or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Ahmed et al. (2022), Semantic probabilistic layers for neuro-symbolic learning, to its existing discussion of control and alignment of deep generative models, with a corresponding bibliography entry. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 6 replaces 'inherently sequential marginalization algorithms' with 'sequential (P-hard) marginalization problems.' v2 also updates publication text and acknowledgements, including SAFRON funding and a public-release statement. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 changes typesetting, spacing, and column/page breaks and adds an ICML proceedings footer on the first page. Figures 1 and 2 retain the same diagrams, illustrative table, and substantive captions.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the final open question more precise by asking about P-hard marginalization problems and modestly expands related-work attribution through Ahmed et al. (2022). These are limited improvements to clarity and context; the core theoretical contributions, worked examples, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.
